1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Nf3 b6 5.e3.strategy: Hits the knight on e4, which nothing protects yet; the pinned knight on c3 cannot take it, so the queen does the work. The queen also guards c3 against the bishop. Black has to support or trade the knight at once.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Nf3 b6 5.e3.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence: St. Petersburg Variation

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Nf3 b6 5.e3.strategy: Guards the knight on e4, which White's queen attacks, and puts the bishop on the long diagonal in the same move. Black keeps the knight on its strong central square and the pin on c3 in place, so White has to spend time challenging the knight rather than developing.
